newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Chirac sees EMU summits overseeing monetary union.
newsitem.headline: Chirac sees EMU summits overseeing monetary union.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Saturday he believed future members of a single European currency would hold regular summits to co-ordinate economic policy and act as a counterweight to the European central bank.

He told a news conference after an EU summit that one of the things that remained to be done in preparation for the launch of a European monetary union was to establish a political authority to balance the monetary power of the central bank.

"In a form which has yet to be determined, the council of ministers and the council of heads of state and government of the countries which are in the euro will constitute this power opposite the central bank," he said.
He said there was general agreement on this point, although ministers have said a call by France for a political body to oversee European monetary union had not been discussed in Dublin.

France has insisted that while the future independent European central bank will control monetary policy, economic policies, including exchange rate policies, will remain firmly in the hands of elected politicians.
Chirac also said that the mumber of countries in a single currency at the start would be "significantly more than is thought".
